title: Custom-designed Cu 2+ - or Ba 2+ -modified clinoptilolite/graphene oxide for the efficient adsorption of sulfur dioxide
content: The flue gas purification technology in the steel industry generates substantial by-products and causes new environmental problems. Dry adsorption enables the integrated removal of multiple pollutants and the recycling of sulfur dioxide (SO2), and it has become one of the most promising methods for pollutant treatment. This paper reports the development of an adsorbent that not only is highly efficient and cost-effective but also possesses strong thermal stability and a large adsorption capacity. The work mainly focuses on clinoptilolite (Cp) and investigates the adsorption characteristics and mechanisms of SO2 on Cu2+- or Ba2+-modified Cp. The properties of several adsorbents are comprehensively evaluated through scanning electron microscopy, N2 adsorption–desorption measurements, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The SO2-saturated adsorption capacity of each material follows the order: Cp-Cu/GO (322.25 mg g−1) > Cp-Ba/GO (320.28 mg g−1) > Cp-Cu (175.83 mg g−1) > Cp-Ba (141.32 mg g−1) > Cp (62.33 mg g−1). Notably, the maximum adsorption capacity reaches 322.25 mg g−1, which is over five times that of Cp. The findings offer valuable theoretical support for the industrial application of such adsorbents.
